- Steer soft-yield: a steering message (user `Ctrl+S`, subagent completion,
  inbox mail) arriving DURING a tool-call phase cancels the phase's
  zone-scoped yield token — `currentYieldToken()` in `cancel_token.dart`,
  published by `_runToolCallPhase` (`agent_loop.dart`), fed by
  `AgentLoopConfig.steeringNotifications` (in-process queue) and the
  non-draining `hasPendingSteering` probe (external inbox, 2s poll).
  Yield-aware tools (`bash`, blocking `task`) finish the tool call early
  WITHOUT stopping the work — it continues as a background job and the user
  message is delivered at the step boundary. Tools ignoring the token keep
  the classic behavior (message waits for the phase).
- `lib/src/messaging/` — the agent messaging fabric: every agent (main,
  subagents, other Fa instances sharing the root) owns a file inbox behind
  the isolated `MessagingRepository` interface (send/peek/drain/directory —
  future DB/network impls drop in without caller changes).
  `AgentMessage.kind` distinguishes agent chat from `user` input handed
  over by an attached client (the Fa app's attach view; the CLI delivers
  it as `[from app] …`, its own words, not agent chat).
  `FileMessagingRepository` over `ExecutionEnv`:
  `<root>/<agent>/inbox|read/<id>.json`, timestamp-ordered names, sanitized
  agent dirs, torn writes skipped. `SubagentManager.messaging` routes
  `enqueueMessage`/`drainMessages` through the fabric (in-memory queue is
  the no-fabric fallback); `mailboxPrefix` (the session id, set by the host
  on every session init/switch) namespaces mailboxes so two instances never
  drain each other — ids with `/` are absolute cross-instance addresses
  (`<sessionId>/main`). Sessions also carry their display NAME
  (`--session goal_builder`): `register(agentId, {sessionName})` persists
  it in a `.name` marker + messages-registry.json, `agent_directory`
  renders `name (id)`, and `agent_message` resolves `goal_builder` /
  `goal_builder/main` through the directory (exact ids/siblings/`main`
  pass through untouched; ambiguous names error with candidates).
  `agent_message` targets siblings, `main`, a session name, or an
  absolute mailbox; `agent_directory` lists LIVE fabric mailboxes (recent
  activity via the heartbeat hosts touch on their inbox-watch timers) plus
  anything with pending mail — stale mailboxes from finished sessions are
  hidden behind the tool's `all: true` (`.id` markers keep real ids despite
  dir sanitization; `_scheduled`/dot-dirs are not mailboxes).
  `schedule_message` (issue #59): records under `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/`;
  self-addressed records deliver to the host's LIVE mailbox at fire time
  (the address pinned at schedule time goes stale on session switch/restart
  and would strand the reminder) — EXCEPT self-addressed records naming a
  subagent mailbox of this session (`<prefix>/<childId>`, gh-970): those
  deliver as recorded (the address rides the same owner prefix and is as
  stable; re-addressing stole the child's reminder into main), and the
  tool's `senderMailbox` override (host-wired from `activeSubagentId()`)
  makes a subagent's no-`to` schedule default to the CHILD's mailbox, not
  main's — hosts re-arm on every mailbox change
  (CLI `_syncMailboxPrefix`, app `_setMailboxPrefix`) and sweep due records
  on their inbox ticks; `dispose()` cancels only the timer, the files stay.
  gh-1180: a re-addressed SELF record also delivers FROM the live mailbox
  (`from` rewritten alongside `to` in `_deliverDueInner`) — an adopted
  reminder keeps the self shape (from == to) the wake policy needs to
  classify it exempt, so a chain survives a session-id change. Every
  lifecycle step lands in the receipt trail
  (`<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl`, `ScheduledReceiptLog`,
  best-effort): scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed
  (queue) and wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused (both hosts'
  wake paths; refusal receipts are once per refusal EPISODE — the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak, so a held gate cannot
  spam the trail and a repeat episode after user input is receipted
  again).
  Sleep resilience (issue #259): all due math rides an injectable wall
  clock (`ScheduledMessageQueue(clock:)`), long waits are split into ≤60s
  timer legs (`maxTimerLeg`) that recompute the remaining delay from the
  wall clock on every fire — never accumulating duration drift — and
  hosts run a catch-up sweep at every TURN START (CLI `_beginUserPrompt`,
  app `sendText`) in addition to the idle inbox ticks, so the first
  post-sleep turn delivers every overdue record immediately. Catch-up is
  exactly-once per record (file removed on send + the `_delivering`
  in-flight guard) — missed cycles of a recurring self-re-arm are NOT
  replayed; the re-armed cycle simply resumes from "now". For true
  sleep-proofing (delivery DURING lid sleep) no in-process timer can
  help: add an external pinger, e.g. a cron/launchd entry that messages
  the session's mailbox — mail to an asleep session already launches a
  headless wake run that drains the inbox and sweeps due records.
 Failure isolation (issue #270): a throwing `send` is contained per
 record (logged via `onError` — CLI `[sched]` line, app `AppLog`), the
 record stays for the next sweep, and the post-failure re-arm floors the
 leg at `failureBackoff` (60s) so a poison record cannot spin a
 zero-delay timer; sweeps deliver in due-time order, and the app's
 turn-start sweep is awaited so the fresh turn sees the fired reminder.
 A failed SCAN (transient `listDir`/read error on a leg, gh-1180) is
 equally loud: `onError` + a `scan_failed` receipt, then a re-arm at
 `failureBackoff` — the arming heartbeat never silently disarms
 ("scan failed" used to be treated as "nothing pending", permanently
 disarming the scheduler with zero log). Corrupt record CONTENT is
 still skipped, not fatal (issue #59). Every lifecycle step is
 receipted to an append-only JSONL trail at
 `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`,
 gh-1180): `scheduled` / `delivered` (with lag) / `delivery_failed` /
 `scan_failed` from the queue, plus host-side `wake_attempted` /
 `turn_started` / `wake_refused` (with reason) from the CLI wake path —
 a post-mortem can distinguish "timer never fired" (no `delivered`)
 from "wake refused" without reading source. The trail is best-effort:
 a failing write logs via `onError` and never breaks scheduling.
 Records carry the scheduling instance's `owner` (mailbox prefix): a
 sweeper re-addresses a self-addressed record only when the stored owner
 matches its own prefix, and never deletes another instance's record -
 foreign-owned records are left where their owner sweeps (also across a
 root change: only own records migrate to an adopted folder's root).
 Legacy untagged records drain via the old any-sweeper path; records
 whose owner session is deleted (`/reset` mints a new id) stay on disk -
 there is no reaper, cleanup is manual. `agent_fabric` resolves the
 messages root lazily per sweep (was: pinned to the launch cwd at
 construction), and pending records migrate across a root change, so a
 session-folder adoption carries the reminders along instead of
 stranding them under the launch cwd.


  The `## Agent messaging` prompt section (prompts messaging_section.md, CLI +
  app variants) tells the model its own mailbox address. Turn-boundary
  delivery: `Agent.externalSteeringSource`
  merges inbox drains into the steering poll (main in AgentCli/AgentService
  as `_mainInboxMessages`, children via the executor) — messages land as
  sender-attributed user messages, so they persist in the session and read
  like a chat. Idle wake: an inbox watcher (2s CLI / 3s app) starts a turn
  when mail arrives while idle — two Fa instances chat live; a 10-run
  streak cap without user input breaks agent-to-agent ping-pong loops.
  The lanes live in `InboxWakePolicy` (gh-1180): user-kind mail always
  wakes and resets the streak (gating it would deadlock:
  no run → no reset → no run); a delivered `schedule_message`
  self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to) is EXEMPT from the
  cap — a deliberate agent-chosen cadence (night watch, periodic sweep)
  wakes forever, with a 30s cadence floor so a zero-delay re-schedule
  spin is still bounded like chatter; foreign agent chatter stays
  capped. A refused wake is never silent: one dim `[mail] wake refused`
  line per episode and a `wake_refused` receipt.
  UI: `/agents` rows show a `mail:N` pending marker (the CLI
  font has no ✉ glyph), the app's AgentsSection shows `✉N`; observe/detail
  views list the pending inbox.

  via delete+add (never left to rot), project scope is PUBLIC (git) —
  no secrets/personal data there, user scope stays machine-local.

  skills/packages); logs/sessions/bash_jobs stay local. Commit memory/
  changes with the task that produced them (`memory:` prefix for
  memory-only commits).

  + JSON-RPC + SSE), `a2a_config.dart` (`a2a:` yaml section, `${NAME}`
  env tokens), `a2a_manager.dart` (lazy per-server connect, A2A task state

- **PR #**: 1810
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1810

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +677
- **Deletions**: -96
- **Created**: 2026-10-23T17:33:58Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-23T17:42:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1809

## feat(1809): CodeMie provider setup — ask for the base URL by default; make project selection real and reachable

### AC table

| AC | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC1 — bare `/provider codemie` asks for the org URL | Done | `_handleCodeMieAuthMethodChoice` prompts `CodeMie URL [https://codemie.lab.epam.com]: ` **before** the auth-method picker; Enter applies the hosted default, a typed URL feeds both SSO and JWT branches. Tests: `bare /provider codemie accepts a custom org URL end-to-end` (SSO branch, asserts the authenticate fn received the typed URL and the entry saved under the custom host), `...shows the URL prompt then the auth-method picker` (Enter-default, JWT branch), `cancels on Ctrl-C and rejects a non-http URL` |
| AC2 — project picker reachable on every SSO connect path | Done | `_applyCodeMieSsoCredentials` no longer short-circuits on `sameAccount`: the guided flow runs for first connect, explicit re-login, expired-cookie switch, startup re-auth, and mid-stream re-auth. A re-login leads the picker with a **keep current project/model** row (Enter keeps the working pair, a pick switches). Tests: `same-account re-login still shows the project picker and the keep-current row preserves the pair`, `re-login finds a renamed entry by base URL...`, `JWT re-login ... leads with the keep-current row` |
| AC3 — failed projects fetch is loud | Done | `_codemiePickProject` catches the fetch error and prints `CodeMie projects fetch failed: <error> — skipping project selection` (tuiWarning), keeping the entry's current project; a genuinely empty (successful) list still skips silently. Test: `a failed projects fetch is loud and the entry has no project` (`/v1/user` → 403 via MockClient) |
| AC4 — project is functional | Done — **FUNCTIONAL form** (see resolution below) | Persists on `CustomProviderEntry.project` (yaml `project:`, null-absent → old configs stay byte-identical) and rides every CodeMie request as the `x-codemie-project` header: SSO switch, JWT switch, saved-entry switch, and startup cookie restore. Tests: first-connect pick persists + header (`first connect picks a project and it persists and rides the requests`), same-account re-login header, JWT header, startup-restore header, yaml round-trip + edit-wizard merge preservation (`custom_providers_test.dart`) |
| AC5 — JWT path gets the project step | Done | `_codemieJwtGuidedSetup` fetches projects via the new `fetchCodeMieProjectsWithJwt` (`Authorization: Bearer` twin of `fetchCodeMieProjects`, extracted shared `_fetchCodeMieProjects` body — extended, not duplicated), then models; same keep-current row on a re-login. Tests: `...jwt saves a custom provider...` + `JWT re-login ... keep-current row` |
| AC6 — regression tests | Done | Line-mode fake-IO (`FakeCliIO` + `waitForIt`) in `test/cli/agent_cli_provider_test.dart` (+1 startup test in `agent_cli_test.dart`, yaml round-trips in `custom_providers_test.dart`); network rides `AgentCliConfig.modelsHttpClient` MockClients (SSO cookie + JWT Bearer variants) |

### AC4 resolution — the CodeMie assistant API DOES accept an active project

**Functional, not informational.** Evidence from the official CodeMie CLI (`codemie-ai/codemie-code`, public repo):

- `src/providers/plugins/sso/proxy/plugins/header-injection.plugin.ts` — every proxied request to the CodeMie backend gets `context.headers['X-CodeMie-Project'] = config.project` (when set), alongside `X-CodeMie-Integration`, `X-CodeMie-Repository`, `X-CodeMie-Session-ID`.
- `src/cli/commands/proxy/connect-orchestrator.ts` — the profile field `codeMieProject` (picked during setup) is wired into the daemon config as `project`, which the header plugin forwards.
- `src/providers/plugins/sso/sso.setup-steps.ts` — setup marks project selection **required** (fail fast) and uses it to scope the LiteLLM integration list (`integration.project_name === selectedProject`) before persisting `codeMieProject`.
- FA's own `fetchCodeMieProjects` already reads the same `/v1/user` `applications`(+admin) contract, and the chat/models traffic rides `/code-assistant-api`, so the header applies to the exact backend FA talks to.

Implementation: the header is attached via the model's `headers` map (`x-codemie-project`) — the same mechanism the SSO `cookie:` header uses, which the openai-completions adapter merges into every request (`openai_completions.dart:915`). Lowercase key matches the repo's existing header-map convention.

### Design notes

- The keep-current row (AC2's sanctioned option) appears exactly when an existing entry serves the endpoint: label `keep current project/model` (or `keep current model` for legacy entries without a project), detail naming the values. Picking it skips the model fetch entirely.
- `config.codeMieGuidedSetupFn` (the test seam) keeps its `modelId`-only contract; overridable flows leave `project` untouched (pinned by the unchanged first-connect override test).
- `mergeEditedCustomProviderEntry` now preserves `project` across wizard edits, like `authMethod`/`authHeader`/the tuning keys before it.

### Gates

- `dart analyze` (standalone SDK, stable channel): clean on all 7 touched files.
- `dart format` (real dartfmt): applied to all touched files.
- Targeted tests (touched suites only, per fleet rules): `agent_cli_provider_test.dart` **77 passed** (incl. all new/reworked CodeMie tests), `agent_cli_test.dart` **84 passed**, `custom_providers_test.dart` **22 passed**, `codemie_sso_test.dart` + `codemie_sso_integration_test.dart` **20 passed**.
- CRAP ratchet (crap4dart 0.17.0, local lcov over the touched suites): worst touched method `_handleCodeMieJwtCommand` 11.50 (< 12.0); `_applyCodeMieSsoCredentials` 10.05; picker trio ≤ 4 CC fully covered. Whole-tree max unchanged.
- Size gate: `provider_commands.dart` 2773 / 2800 lines (the project-pick cluster moved into `codemie_provider_commands.dart`, its dedicated file).
- Parity: `project` is a `customProviders` **per-entry** key — covered by the section-level registration (`SharedSetting.customProviders`, `yamlKeys: ['customProviders']`), same precedent as `authHeader` (#964), per-entry `connectTimeoutMs` (#1398), `keyNotPersisted` (gh-1679). No registry/SKILL.md change needed.

### Disclosures

- CI-DISPATCH BAN respected: no workflow runs dispatched; bare head is normal, the owner's SM schedules CI.
- Local CRAP numbers use a single-shard lcov (the 5 suites above), not CI's merged lcov — cross-shard-covered methods (copilot/chatgpt flows in the same files) show N/A locally; nothing I touched relies on that.
- The mid-stream expired-cookie re-auth (`_handleCodeMieAuthExpired`) now also reaches the picker after the browser flow — the AC2 list includes expired-cookie re-authorization; Enter on the keep-current row preserves the exact previous behavior.
- Live behavioral verification could not run against the real CodeMie deployment (auth-gated EPAM host) — the MockClient suites drive the real flow code end-to-end (REPL line loop → guided pickers → registry persistence → model headers), and the request-time header contract is cross-checked against the official CLI source quoted above.

🚨 **BLOCKING: JWT-path projects fetch requests a doubled `/v1` — the AC5 project picker is dead against the real backend**

`_handleCodeMieJwtCommand` builds `apiBase` **with** `/v1` already appended:

```dart
final apiBase = '${codeMieApiBase(orgUrl)}/v1';   // …/code-assistant-api/v1
```

and passes it into `_codemieJwtGuidedSetup` → `_codemiePickProject` → `fetchCodeMieProjectsWithJwt(apiBase, …)`, which appends **another** `/v1/user`:

```dart
return _fetchCodeMieProjects('$apiBase/v1/user', {…}, client);
```

The two helpers have different `apiBase` conventions — `fetchCodeMieModels`/`fetchCodeMieModelsWithJwt` expect `<org>/code-assistant-api/v1` (they append `/llm_models`), while `fetchCodeMieProjects`/`fetchCodeMieProjectsWithJwt` expect `<org>/code-assistant-api` (they append `/v1/user`). The SSO path feeds the project step the no-`/v1` form (`credentials.apiUrl` = `codeMieApiBase(...)`), so it is correct; the JWT path feeds the `/v1` form, producing:

- **JWT path (this PR)**: `GET …/code-assistant-api/v1/v1/user` ❌
- **SSO path (pre-existing)**: `GET …/code-assistant-api/v1/user` ✅

I verified this mechanically against the real code on the PR branch (probe running `fetchCodeMieProjectsWithJwt` through a `MockClient`):

```
JWT path requests : https://codemie.lab.epam.com/code-assistant-api/v1/v1/user
SSO path requests : https://codemie.lab.epam.com/code-assistant-api/v1/user
```

**Impact**: against the real CodeMie backend this endpoint 404s, `_fetchCodeMieProjects` throws `ConfigException('CodeMie user info failed (404)')`, and `_codemiePickProject`'s AC3 catch fires `CodeMie projects fetch failed: … — skipping project selection` on **every** JWT connect. AC5's project step can never work in production; every JWT user gets the loud failure branch instead of the picker.

**Why CI is green**: `_codeMieJwtMockClient` matches with `url.contains('/v1/user')`, and `…/v1/v1/user` still *contains* `/v1/user` — the doubled URL hits the mock's projects branch, so the AC5 test (`…jwt saves a custom provider…`, `JWT re-login … keep-current row`) passes against the wrong URL.

**Fix** (either shape works):
- pass the no-`/v1` root to the project step only, e.g. in `_handleCodeMieJwtCommand` keep `apiRoot = codeMieApiBase(orgUrl)` for `_codemiePickProject` and `'${apiRoot}/v1'` for the models call; or
- normalize inside `_fetchCodeMieProjects`/the JWT twin (collapse a trailing `/v1` before appending `/v1/user`).

Then tighten both mocks to assert the exact request URL (see the companion thread on `_codeMieSsoMockClient`) so this shape cannot regress green again.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: route matchers use `url.contains(...)` — URL-shape regressions pass green**

The new `_codeMieSsoMockClient` (and the pre-existing `_codeMieJwtMockClient` at line 2906) dispatch on substring matches:

```dart
if (url.contains('/v1/user')) { … }
if (url.contains('/llm_models')) { … }
```

A `contains` matcher cannot distinguish `…/v1/user` from `…/v1/v1/user` — which is exactly why the JWT-path double-`/v1` bug in this PR ships with a fully green suite (see the companion 🚨 thread on `fetchCodeMieProjectsWithJwt`).

Suggest asserting the exact request URL in both mocks, e.g.:

```dart
if (request.url.toString() == '$apiBase/v1/user') { … }
```

with `apiBase` built the same way the production code builds it (`codeMieApiBase(orgUrl)` for the SSO path, `'${codeMieApiBase(orgUrl)}/v1'` for the JWT path). That turns any future path-convention mistake into a red test naming the actual URL instead of a silently-degraded feature.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `__keep-current__` sentinel can collide with a real project name**

`_pickCodeMieProject` uses the string sentinel `_codeMieKeepCurrent = '__keep-current__'` as the picker key of the keep-current row, and every fetched project is listed with its own name as the key:

```dart
for (final p in projects) (p, p, ''),
```

If the CodeMie backend ever returns a project literally named `__keep-current__`, selecting that row would be interpreted as "keep current" and silently keep the old pair instead of switching. Extremely unlikely, but cheap to make impossible: filter the sentinel out of `projects` before building the list, or key the rows by index and map back. Fine to defer — just noting it since the sentinel now guards a persisted decision.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the edit-wizard merge carries `project` across a `baseUrl` change too**

`mergeEditedCustomProviderEntry` now preserves `project` unconditionally, mirroring `authMethod`/`authHeader`/the tuning keys:

```dart
..project = existing.project;
```

`project` differs from those in one respect: it is a value scoped to the *endpoint* (a project of org A means nothing to org B). If the wizard edit changes `baseUrl` — say from `codemie.lab.epam.com` to a second org — the old org's project name survives the merge and rides the new org's requests as `x-codemie-project`. The server will most likely ignore an unknown project, so this is low-harm, but a one-line guard would keep the pair coherent:

```dart
..project = sameEndpoint(existing.baseUrl, updated.baseUrl)
    ? existing.project
    : null;
```

(`sameEndpoint` already lives in this file.) Optional — the next guided connect overwrites it either way.

diff = open('/tmp/full_diff.txt').read()

cur = None
for line in diff.splitlines():

    if h and cur:

        for i in range(start, start+n): newlines[cur].add(i)
        continue
    if cur and (line.startswith('+') or line.startswith(' ')) and not line.startswith('+++'):
        # right-side counter already populated by the hunk range; nothing extra
        pass

    ok = ln in newlines.get(p, set())
